regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% is the headline; the quality test is IIP at 6.7% — down from 8.8% — with capital goods the lone bright spot at 16.1%. PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) looks solid until you notice manufacturing slipped to 52.8 from 53.5 while services carried the composite; an economy where services PMI does the heavy lifting while factory output decelerates is not firing on all cylinders. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up from 75.6% — is the one number that earns genuine optimism: private capex rarely accelerates below 75%, and we are now above that threshold for the first time in six quarters.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"CPI at 4.45% is 45bps above the RBI's midpoint target, but the decomposition is what matters: core at 3.9% (28th percentile) is benign, food at 5.52% is manageable, and fuel at 22.93% (95th percentile) is the trapdoor. WPI at 9.92% — 270bps above CPI — signals producer-level pressure that has not yet fully transmitted to consumers; with Brent rising five consecutive months to $108.72, that transmission is a question of when, not whether. RBI's own inflation forecast just jumped from 4.6% to 5.1% — a 50bps revision in a single cycle — which is the clearest signal that the rate-cut narrative the market is pricing is built on a foundation that the RBI itself no longer believes.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — is the structural fault line of this cycle. CD ratio at 81.4% has pulled back from 82.5%, but the direction of travel in credit (13.7% → 14.5% → 17.1%) versus flat deposits means the gap is widening in flow terms even as the stock ratio ticks down. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% with credit accelerating was FY14; within 12 months, the taper tantrum forced 75bps of emergency rate hikes — today's setup rhymes, except the external shock (US 10Y at 4.95%) is already arriving. NBFC credit growth jumping from 10.6% to 14.9% is not a sign of system health; it is banks pushing risk to the shadow system because their own balance sheets are deposit-constrained.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% with CPI at 4.45% and RBI's own forecast at 5.1% means the real rate is approximately 15bps — barely positive, and likely to go negative if fuel inflation transmits fully into headline. RBI is on hold, but the market pricing a cut is reading a forecast the RBI just revised upward by 50bps; that is a positioning error waiting to be corrected. For housing, the average home loan rate at 8.35% against an affordability index at a 19th-percentile 3.5 means EMI-to-income ratios are already stretched — any rate hike from here compresses demand in the one sector where credit growth (11.3% YoY) is already the slowest across all categories.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% and capacity utilisation at 77.4% are the two numbers that validate the capex upcycle as real, not budgetary. Credit to industry accelerating from 6.5% to 20% YoY — and credit to services from 10.2% to 22.9% — confirms corporates are borrowing to build, not to refinance legacy debt. The inversion to test: core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) with steel and cement showing base-effect softness — if this is genuinely base effects, cement dispatch data over the next two months will confirm; if core sector stays below 5.5% into Q3, the capex story is more government-led than the IIP capital goods number suggests.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 crore is 14.8% above the prior month's ₹1,74,116 crore — but April advance filings and year-end compliance bunching explain a material portion of the beat; the 10-year percentile of 71% is solid but not exceptional. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% are the cleaner consumption signal: two-wheelers are the rural and semi-urban proxy, and 19.7% growth at a 55th-percentile level suggests the mass market is participating, not just the affluent tier. The tension worth watching: e-commerce GMV growth at 18% (26th percentile) is the weakest of the consumption indicators — urban discretionary spending online is growing at a pace that would have been considered disappointing in FY22, even as physical retail and auto sales look strong.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 630bps divergence that has widened for three consecutive months (13.7% → 14.5% → 17.1% credit; deposits lagging). CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month) masks the underlying stress: banks are funding the gap via wholesale markets and RBI liquidity windows. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% (from 10.6%) signals desperation for alternative funding sources.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they'll poach deposits from weaker peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; liquidity tightening will force margin compression. Watch for RBI to signal a rate cut within 2-3 months to ease funding stress. Reduce exposure to smaller PSU banks dependent on government deposits.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically preceded either RBI rate cuts or credit rationing. The last time credit-deposit divergence exceeded 600bps (2022), RBI cut rates 250bps within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up from 75.6% prior month) signals capex momentum is real. Core sector growth at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) is the only soft spot, but this reflects base effects in steel/cement — not demand weakness. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (from 6.5% prior) and credit to services at 22.9% (from 10.2%) confirm corporates are borrowing to invest, not refinance.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, industrial machinery, and cement stocks. Increase allocation to project-linked equities (L&T, Thermax, Cummins). Private capex is leading; public capex will follow. Avoid consumer discretionary until capex cycle matures (12-18 months out). Hedge with long-duration bonds — capex-driven growth will eventually push inflation higher and force RBI to hold rates.","pct_10y":52,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is mid-cycle; historically, capex accelerates most aggressively when CU moves from 75% to 82%. This cycle has 500-700bps of upside.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Affluent Money Entering Via SIP Backdoor","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (Mar 2026, 10y: 92nd percentile) with SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (82nd percentile) but SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (93rd percentile). The divergence is stark: accounts growing 1.2% MoM but AUM growing 2.3% MoM. Average SIP ticket size is rising — affluent investors are using SIP as a tax-efficient entry vehicle, not mass retail. DII equity net flows at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile, all-time high) and MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (86th percentile) confirm domestic money is rotating into equities.","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour. Affluent retail entering via SIP signals they believe the rally has legs but want downside protection via systematic entry. Reduce new equity allocations; take profits on 12-month winners. Rotate into quality large-cap defensives (HDFC Bank, TCS, ITC). Avoid small-cap and mid-cap momentum plays — they'll underperform when SIP growth normalises. Watch for SIP YoY growth (currently 14%, down from 16%) to turn negative — that's your exit signal.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile preceded market corrections in 2018 and 2022. When affluent money enters via SIP at these levels, retail euphoria typically peaks 3-6 months later.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Oil Shock Brewing; Fuel Inflation Uncontrollable","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% (up from 20.05% prior month, 95th percentile) with WTI at $103.75 (85th percentile, up 3 of last 5 months) and Brent at $108.72 (75th percentile, rising 5 consecutive months). India's import bill for crude is accelerating; at current prices, India's CAD will widen 50-80bps. CPI headline at 4.45% (up from 4.38%) is being held down only by food deflation (CFPI at 5.52%, up from 5.32% but still manageable). If oil breaks $115/bbl, headline CPI will spike to 5.2%+ and force RBI to abandon rate-cut hopes.","implication":"Hedge INR weakness — oil shocks always weaken the rupee. Reduce exposure to refiners (IOCL, BPCL) unless they have hedges in place. Overweight energy importers with pricing power (Pharma, IT services). Avoid consumer staples with high oil-linked input costs. Build a long-dated oil put spread ($100-$110 strike) to protect against further CAD deterioration. Monitor OPEC+ production cuts — any extension signals $120+ oil by Q3 2026.","pct_10y":85,"pct_note":"WTI at 85th percentile historically preceded 200-300bps of INR depreciation within 3 months. Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is unsustainable and will force policy tightening.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"US Rates Spike; Carry Trade Unravelling","data_text":"US 10Y Treasury at 4.95% (89th percentile, up 4 of last 5 months, recent: 4.64→4.77) with Fed funds at 3.63% (flat). BOJ rate at 1.0% (86th percentile, up from 0.75%, strong-negative signal: -72) signals Japan is tightening. DXY at 99.65 (flat but up 3 of last 5 months) is holding firm. The carry trade (borrow JPY at 1%, invest in USD at 4.95%) is compressing — yen strength will force deleveraging of India-linked carry positions. US GDP at 1.5% SAAR (down from 2.1%) signals US growth is slowing into higher rates — a toxic combination for emerging markets.","implication":"Reduce FII equity exposure; foreign flows will reverse when US rates stay elevated. Hedge INR via long-dated USD calls (96-98 strike). Avoid high-beta EM plays (small-cap, infrastructure). Rotate into large-cap defensives with USD earnings (TCS, Infosys, Pharma). Watch for US 10Y to break 5.0% — that's the trigger for a 2-3% INR depreciation and ₹5,000 Cr+ FII outflow. Position for a 200bps INR move (95.24 → 97.50) over 6 months.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 89th percentile preceded EM currency crises in 2013 and 2018. BOJ tightening at this pace is historically associated with yen carry unwind and 300-500bps of EM currency depreciation.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakening; RBI Reserves Under Pressure","data_text":"INR/USD at 95.24 (down from 95.54, 89th percentile, recent: 95.24→96.15→95.24→96.15→95.24→94.34 showing 2-way volatility but uptrend intact). FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (83rd percentile) is masking outflows in debt — total FII flows are likely negative. RBI's intervention (evidenced by INR holding 95.24 despite US 10Y spike) is burning reserves. At current pace of intervention, RBI's usable reserves (ex-gold) will decline ₹30-40 Bn per month.","implication":"INR will test 96.50 within 2 months if US 10Y stays above 4.90%. RBI will defend 96.00 but will eventually allow depreciation to 97.00-98.00 to preserve reserves. Corporates should lock in USD hedges now (6-12 month forwards at 96.50-97.00). Avoid INR-denominated bonds; duration risk is rising. Overweight exporters (IT, Pharma, Textiles) — INR weakness is a tailwind. Reduce import-heavy sectors (Auto, Chemicals).","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile historically preceded 200-300bps of further depreciation. RBI's reserve adequacy (months of imports) is declining; at current burn rate, RBI will be forced to allow INR to weaken to 97.50+ by Q3 2026.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Pivot","data_text":"Office absorption at 29.9 Mn sqft (down from 28.2 prior, but recent: 29.9→26.9→13.7 showing a 2-month collapse of 54%). Office vacancy at 13.9% (down from 17.2%, but recent: 13.9→14.5→14.7 rising 2 in a row). Nifty IT is flat (recent: 24080→24056→23914→23873→23898→23779, down 1.3% over 6 months) despite 16% credit growth to services sector. The disconnect: traditional IT services are NOT driving office demand. Global Capability Centers (GCCs) — captive R&D units of MNCs — are the real buyer, and they're consolidating into fewer, larger campuses. This means commercial RE is decoupling from the IT stock proxy.","implication":"Sell Nifty IT on any bounce — the sector is losing its real estate tailwind. Overweight commercial RE plays (Embassy REIT, Mindspace REIT) that cater to GCCs, not IT services. GCC consolidation will drive premium office rents (₹125+/sqft in Mumbai, ₹100+/sqft in Bengaluru) but will crater mid-tier office absorption. Avoid IT services stocks with large real estate footprints (TCS, Infosys) — they'll face margin pressure from underutilised campuses. Watch for Q4 FY26 earnings: if IT services report flat/negative office utilisation, the stock repricing will be severe (15-20% downside).","pct_10y":24,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 24th percentile is historically associated with commercial RE downturns. The last time absorption collapsed this sharply (2020-21), office REITs underperformed by 30-40% while GCC-focused landlords outperformed by 50%+. This cycle is repeating.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with a 54.6 composite PMI looks like an economy in fine health — until IIP at 6.7% (down from 8.8%) reveals that factory output is decelerating even as the headline accelerates. Capacity utilisation crossing 77.4% — the threshold above which private capex historically responds — is the single most credible forward indicator in today's data set; credit to industry jumping from 6.5% to 20% YoY confirms corporates are acting on it. Fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile) is the regime's central contradiction: consumption is strong enough to absorb it today, but RBI's own forecast revision to 5.1% signals the institution no longer believes the benign path. Growth is real; its durability depends on whether Brent at $108.72 — rising five consecutive months — breaks the consumer before the capex cycle matures.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

4.95% on the US 10Y — up four of the last five months and at an 89th-percentile reading — is the single most important number for India today, because it is repricing the cost of every dollar of EM carry simultaneously. US GDP at 1.5% SAAR (down from 2.1%) means the Fed is holding rates into a slowing economy — the toxic combination that historically precedes EM capital flow reversals, not orderly rotations. BOJ at 1.0% (up from 0.75%) is compressing the JPY carry trade that has funded a portion of EM inflows for three years; yen strength forces deleveraging, and India-linked positions are not immune. China at 4.3% GDP growth with a composite PMI of 49.5 — still below 50 — removes the one engine that could have offset US demand softness for Asian exporters.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII equity net flows at ₹58,502 crore — a 100th-percentile, all-time high — are absorbing what FII equity inflows of ₹29,631 crore (83rd percentile) are not telling you: FII debt flows are likely negative, and total foreign flows are probably flat to negative once fixed income is included. SIP inflows at ₹32,297 crore with AUM growing at 2.3% MoM against account growth of only 1.2% MoM signals rising average ticket size — affluent investors are deploying larger tranches via SIP, not new retail participants entering the market. Bank deposit growth at 10.8% against credit at 17.1% means the system is funding a 630bps gap via wholesale markets and RBI windows — a structural liquidity drain that will eventually force either deposit rate hikes or credit rationing. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 crore at a 0th-percentile reading suggests the capital market is not yet an effective relief valve for the deposit gap.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Nifty at 23,398 — down from a recent 24,080, falling four of the last five periods — is pricing a soft landing that the US 10Y at 4.95% and BOJ at 1.0% are jointly contesting; Bank Nifty at 56,607 (93rd percentile) is the most exposed, because NIM compression from deposit rate wars — the inevitable second-order effect of an 81.4% CD ratio — has not yet appeared in earnings. Office REITs tell the starkest story: Embassy, Mindspace, and Brookfield are down 16%, 30%, and 21% respectively from prior readings, even as office absorption at 29.9 mn sqft masks a two-month sequential collapse from 29.9 → 26.9 → 13.7 mn sqft — the GCC consolidation thesis means fewer, larger deals, not a demand recovery. Residential real estate launches at 106,000 units outpacing sales at 90,715 units — with unsold inventory at 616,000 units — is the supply-demand mismatch that a home loan rate of 8.35% and a 19th-percentile affordability index will not resolve without price correction.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Ranked by probability × impact: first, Brent at $108.72 breaking $115/bbl — a 5.8% move from here — triggers CPI at 5.2%+, forces RBI to abandon any residual easing bias, and widens CAD by 50-80bps, putting the INR's 95.24 floor under genuine stress. Second, US 10Y sustaining above 5.0% — just 5bps away — accelerates EM carry unwind, pressures RBI's usable reserves (declining an estimated ₹30-40bn/month at current intervention pace), and converts FII equity inflows into outflows within one to two months. Third, the CD ratio at 81.4% with credit accelerating to 17.1% forces a macro-prudential response — risk weight hikes on unsecured and NBFC lending — that would compress credit growth by 200-300bps and stall the capex upcycle before it self-sustains. Watch Thursday's RBI liquidity data and the weekly credit-deposit release — if the gap widens beyond 650bps, the probability of a macro-prudential circular before year-end rises sharply.

"}
